incidente.resumo: An attacker obtained remote access using RDP to a computer of a customer support engineer at Okta sub-processor Sitel, a machine logged into Okta, and could take screenshots and control it; the threat actor had access to the Sitel environment during a five-day window in January 2022; screenshots were published online by LAPSUS$ in March 2022. Okta states its service was not breached and puts the maximum potential impact at 366 customers whose tenants were accessed by Sitel. After an alert, Okta terminated the engineer's Okta sessions and suspended the account.
servicos_afetados: Okta customer tenants accessed by Sitel

descricao.texto: On January 20, 2022 at 23:18 UTC, Okta Security received an alert that a new factor (a password) was added to a Sitel employee's Okta account from a new location.
trechos: January 20, 2022, 23:18 - Okta Security received an alert that a new factor was added to a Sitel employee’s Okta account from a new location.

descricao.texto: An attacker obtained remote access using RDP to a Sitel support engineer's computer, owned and managed by Sitel, that was logged into Okta, and was able to take screenshots and control the machine through the RDP session; the attacker never gained access to the Okta service via account takeover. The forensic report found the threat actor had access to the Sitel environment between January 16 and 21, 2022. The text does not say how the remote access was obtained.
trechos: Our investigation determined that the screenshots, which were not contained in the Sitel summary report, were taken from a Sitel support engineer’s computer upon which an attacker had obtained remote access using RDP. This device was owned and managed by Sitel.

So while the attacker never gained access to the Okta service via account takeover, a machine that was logged into Okta was compromised and they were able to obtain screenshots and control the machine through the RDP session.

The report from the forensic firm highlighted that there was a five-day window of time between January 16-21, 2022 when the threat actor had access to the Sitel environment, which we validated with our own analysis.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: A long period passed between Okta's notification to Sitel and the complete investigation report: the forensic report to Sitel was dated March 10, Okta received a summary report on March 17 that did not contain the screenshots, and the complete report on March 22, after the screenshots were published; Okta says it should have moved more swiftly once it received the summary report.
trechos: January 21, 2022, to March 10, 2022 - The forensic firm’s investigation and analysis of the incident was conducted until February 28, 2022, with its report to Sitel dated March 10, 2022.
March 17, 2022 - Okta received a summary report about the incident from Sitel
March 22, 2022, at 03:30 - Screenshots shared online by LAPSUS$
March 22, 2022, at 12:27 - Okta received the complete investigation report from Sitel

I am greatly disappointed by the long period of time that transpired between our notification to Sitel and the issuance of the complete investigation report. Upon reflection, once we received the Sitel summary report we should have moved more swiftly to understand its implications.

Our investigation determined that the screenshots, which were not contained in the Sitel summary report, were taken from a Sitel support engineer’s computer upon which an attacker had obtained remote access using RDP.

passos.texto: After the alert, the Sitel engineer's Okta account was reset; on January 21, 2022 at 00:28 UTC the Okta Service Desk terminated the user's Okta sessions and suspended the account until the root cause of the suspicious activity could be identified and remediated.
trechos: On January 20, 2022, the Okta Security team was alerted that a new factor was added to a Sitel customer support engineer’s Okta account.
Although that individual attempt was unsuccessful, out of an abundance of caution, we reset the account and notified Sitel who engaged a leading forensic firm to perform an investigation.
January 21, 2022, at 00:28 - The Okta Service Desk terminated the user’s Okta sessions and suspended the account until the root cause of suspicious activity could be identified and remediated.

acoes.texto: Okta states there are many opportunities to improve its processes and communications, without naming specific actions.
trechos: As with all security incidents, there are many opportunities for us to improve our processes and our communications.

motivo_confianca_baixa: triagem.tipo: postmortem vs atualizacoes_status. The text calls itself an update ('This update was posted at 8:50 AM') and links to 'previous updates and public statements', which fits 'updates published during the incident... If the document contains status updates at all, this wins over postmortem'; but it was written two months after the intrusion ended and is a company blog post entirely about one incident, which fits 'postmortem'. Whether the ongoing public investigation counts as 'during the incident' is not decided by the definitions.
observacoes: The five-day window (January 16-21, 2022) is the period of attacker access, not a service outage, so duracao is null. The MFA challenge on the new factor was not accepted, preventing access to the Okta account. The screenshots were shared online by LAPSUS$ on March 22, 2022, and Okta determined that day that they were related to the January incident. Okta states that support engineer access through SuperUser is limited (they cannot create or delete users, download customer databases or access source code), that no customer corrective actions are needed, and that the 366 potentially impacted customers will receive a report of the actions Sitel performed on their tenants.
